nodes.reading:
Why a system optimizing on its own map cannot see the map; why coherence — not rationality — is the mode that sees it; and why a purely maximizing agent is structurally blind to exactly the capabilities that keep a system alive.

Document Status — Working Paper 2 · Series: Informational Friction (a systems theory)

Builds on Paper 1 ( The Map and the Flow ), which established the object: a representation used as a control surface, diverging from the flow it governs, with back-action. This paper supplies the agent-level mechanism beneath that object. The forward forecasts (the Outlook) and the consolidated falsification battery are deferred to later papers in the series; falsifiable claims are marked inline.

nodes.title: Why Selection Cannot See It
nodes.reading:
Insolvency, positive deviation, and a case (Nokia) in which market and evolutionary predictions pointed confidently in the wrong direction — the case that motivates the claim that the two instruments are complementary, not rival. Why selection does not refute this theory; it nests inside it.

Builds on Paper 1 ( The Map and the Flow ) and Paper 2 ( Rationality, Coherence, and the Frame ). This paper supplies the dynamics — insolvency and the closed-system destiny — and the central defense: the rival most likely to topple the theory, evolutionary / market selection, does not reach it. Nokia is the witnessed, motivating case used to show the two instruments are complementary, not rival; it is not a causal account of why any firm declined. The forward forecasts (the Outlook) and the consolidated falsification battery are deferred to later papers in the series; falsifiable claims are marked inline.

The territorial dimension makes the frame explicit: an operating outcome must be evaluated against the affected recipients and obligations, not only the contractor's local target.
The case-study framework can preserve the field observation as evidence while recording the migration interpretation as a separate, testable layer with its own data requirements.
